+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler
+
+
+def _input_batch(req_ids: list[str], structured: bool) -> InputBatch:
+    num_reqs = len(req_ids)
+    buffers = InputBuffers(num_reqs, num_reqs, torch.device("cuda"))
+    batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, buffers, is_padding=False)
+    return replace(batch, req_ids=req_ids, has_structured_output_reqs=structured)
+
+
+def _set_draft_toks(
+    handler: DraftTokensHandler,
+    req_ids: list[str],
+    tokens: list[list[int]],
+    structured: bool,
+) -> None:
+    batch = _input_batch(req_ids=req_ids, structured=structured)
+    handler.set_draft_tokens(batch, torch.tensor(tokens, device="cuda"))
+
+
+def _get_draft_toks(handler: DraftTokensHandler) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
+    drafts = handler.get_draft_tokens()
+    assert drafts is not None
+    return dict(zip(drafts.req_ids, drafts.draft_token_ids, strict=True))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+def test_draft_tokens_follow_request_lifecycle() -> None:
+    handler = DraftTokensHandler(torch.device("cuda"))
+
+    # The worker samples two structured-output requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[11, 12], [21, 22]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+
+    # "b" finishes before this result is handed back to the scheduler
+    handler.discard("b")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {"a": [11, 12]}
+
+    # "a" continues and "b" is re-added with a new draft row
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[13, 14], [23, 24]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+    }
+
+    # A batch without structured-output must not erase drafts from live requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["plain"],
+        tokens=[[31, 32]],
+        structured=False,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+
+    # Requests finish independently, and the handler is empty once all are gone
+    handler.discard("a")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+    handler.discard("b")
+    handler.discard("plain")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {}

+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import MambaAttentionBackendEnum
 from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    FullAttentionSpec,
     KVCacheConfig,
     KVCacheGroupSpec,
     KVCacheLayout,
     KVCacheTensor,
+    MambaSpec,
     MLAAttentionSpec,
+    SlidingWindowSpec,
+    SparseCacheRole,
     create_kv_cache_views,
 )
 
@@ -1840,3 +1845,379 @@ def test_shared_base_regions_with_distinct_block_lens_stay_separate():
     np.testing.assert_array_equal(
         descs[:, 0], [base[0], base[0] + 256, base[0], base[0] + 256]
     )
+
+
+# Real model KV layouts, end to end on CPU: vLLM's planner and allocator build
+# P's and D's caches, D reads one request from P, and the recorded descriptors
+# are run as memory copies so every byte can be checked. Each case is the
+# first layers of a model with that model's per-layer KV specs. Hybrid block
+# sizes are the ones vLLM aligns to on CPU, where the attention page must hold
+# the Mamba state.
+_BF16 = torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _attn(heads, head, head_v=None, window=None):
+    def make(block_size, _mamba_page):
+        kwargs = dict(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=heads,
+            head_size=head,
+            head_size_v=head_v or head,
+            dtype=_BF16,
+        )
+        if window is not None:
+            return SlidingWindowSpec(sliding_window=window, **kwargs)
+        return FullAttentionSpec(**kwargs)
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _mla(head=576, dtype=_BF16, **kwargs):
+    def make(block_size, _mamba_page):
+        return MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=head,
+            dtype=dtype,
+            **kwargs,
+        )
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _mamba(shapes, mamba_type):
+    def make(block_size, mamba_page):
+        return MambaSpec(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            shapes=shapes,
+            dtypes=(_BF16, torch.float32),
+            page_size_padded=mamba_page,
+            mamba_type=mamba_type,
+        )
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _layers(n, make):
+    return [entry for i in range(n) for entry in make(i)]
+
+
+_GDN = MambaAttentionBackendEnum.GDN_ATTN
+# (block size, [(layer name, spec factory)]) per model.
+_REAL_MODELS = {
+    # GLM-4.5-Air and MiniMax-M2 have the same attention shape.
+    "Qwen3-8B": (
+        128,
+        _layers(4, lambda i: [(f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _attn(8, 128))]),
+    ),
+    "gpt-oss-20b": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            4,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.attn.attn",
+                    _attn(8, 64, window=None if i % 2 else 128),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "gemma-3-1b": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            12,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _attn(1, 256, window=None if i % 6 == 5 else 512),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "MiMo-V2-Flash": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            12,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _attn(4, 192, 128)
+                    if i in (0, 5, 11)
+                    else _attn(8, 192, 128, window=128),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    # Kimi-K2 has the same MLA cache.
+    "DeepSeek-V3": (
+        128,
+        _layers(4, lambda i: [(f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _mla())]),
+    ),
+    "DeepSeek-V3.2": (
+        64,
+        _layers(
+            4,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _mla(is_index_group_leader=True),
+                ),
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.indexer.k_cache",
+                    _mla(132, torch.uint8, cache_role=SparseCacheRole.INDEXER),
+                ),
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B": (
+        1152,
+        _layers(
+            8,
+            lambda i: [
+                (f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _attn(2, 256))
+                if i % 4 == 3
+                else (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.linear_attn",
+                    _mamba(((8192, 3), (32, 128, 128)), _GDN),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2": (
+        1408,
+        _layers(
+            22,
+            lambda i: (
+                [
+                    (
+                        f"model.layers.{i}.mixer",
+                        _mamba(
+                            ((12288, 3), (128, 80, 128)),
+                            MambaAttentionBackendEnum.MAMBA2,
+                        ),
+                    )
+                ]
+                if i in (0, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 20)
+                else [(f"model.layers.{i}.mixer.attn", _attn(8, 128))]
+                if i in (14, 21)
+                else []
+            ),
+        ),
+    ),
+    # KDA at 1-based layers 1-3, 5-7; MLA at 4 and 8. A 1920-token MLA page
+    # (64-token kernel blocks) is the first to hold the 2,170,880 B KDA state.
+    "Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B": (
+        1920,
+        _layers(
+            8,
+            lambda i: [
+                (f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _mla())
+                if i % 4 == 3
+                else (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn",
+                    _mamba(((12288, 3), (32, 128, 128)), _GDN),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+}
+_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE = ["LBNHC", "LBHNC", "BLNHC", "BLHNC", "BHLNC", "LHBNC"]
+
+
+def _real_model_side(model, layout):
+    """Plan and allocate one side's KV caches the way the engine does, with
+    just enough blocks for one request of one or two blocks per group."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import resolve_kv_cache_layout
+    from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import (
+        get_global_kv_cache_groups,
+        get_kv_cache_configs,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.worker.utils import allocate_kv_cache
+
+    block_size, layers = _REAL_MODELS[model]
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size, max_model_len=block_size, kv_role="kv_both"
+    )
+    vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len = block_size
+    vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = layout
+    vllm_config.kv_transfer_config.kv_buffer_device = "cuda"
+    # A Mamba page is padded to the attention page, which holds it.
+    specs = {name: make(block_size, None) for name, make in layers}
+    mamba_page = max(
+        (
+            spec.page_size_bytes
+            for spec in specs.values()
+            if not isinstance(spec, MambaSpec)
+        ),
+        default=None,
+    )
+    specs = {name: make(block_size, mamba_page) for name, make in layers}
+    resolved = resolve_kv_cache_layout(
+        vllm_config, [_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE], specs.values()
+    )
+    groups = get_global_kv_cache_groups(vllm_config, [specs])
+    vllm_config.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks_override = 2 + sum(
+        _blocks_per_request(g.kv_cache_spec) for g in groups
+    )
+    kv_cache_config = get_kv_cache_configs(vllm_config, [specs], [1 << 40], groups)[0]
+    kv_cache_config.kv_cache_layout = vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout
+    caches = allocate_kv_cache(
+        kv_cache_config,
+        torch.device("cpu"),
+        resolved,
+        [g.kv_cache_spec.block_size for g in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups],
+    )
+    return vllm_config, kv_cache_config, caches
+
+
+def _blocks_per_request(spec):
+    return 1 if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec) else 2
+
+
+def _real_model_worker(engine_id, vllm_config, kv_cache_config, caches):
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.worker import (
+        NixlConnectorWorker,
+    )
+
+    use_mla = any(
+        isinstance(g.kv_cache_spec, MLAAttentionSpec)
+        for g in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups
+    )
+    fake_backend = MagicMock()
+    fake_backend.get_name.return_value = "FLASHMLA" if use_mla else "FLASH_ATTN"
+    fake_backend.full_cls_name.return_value = "fake.backend"
+    fake_platform = MagicMock()
+    fake_platform.device_type = "cuda"
+    fake_platform.get_nixl_memory_type.return_value = "VRAM"
+    with (
+        patch.object(bw, "NixlWrapper", _RecordingNixl),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_tensor_model_parallel_rank", return_value=0),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size", return_value=1),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_current_attn_backends", return_value=[fake_backend]),
+        patch.object(bw, "select_common_block_size", lambda size, *_: size),
+        patch.object(bw, "current_platform", fake_platform),
+        patch(
+            "vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils.get_conv_state_layout",
+            return_value="DS",
+        ),
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+    ):
+        worker = NixlConnectorWorker(vllm_config, engine_id, kv_cache_config)
+        worker.use_mla = use_mla
+        worker.register_kv_caches(caches)
+    return worker
+
+
+def _cache_pages(cache, block):
+    """A layer's page(s) for one block: one tensor, or one per Mamba state."""
+    return (
+        [c[block] for c in cache]
+        if isinstance(cache, (list, tuple))
+        else [cache[block]]
+    )
+
+

+def test_dequantize_nvfp4_moe_weights_chunked_matches_full(
+    experts_per_chunk: int, invert_global_scales: bool, monkeypatch

+    """Chunked dequantization must equal the single-chunk dequantization exactly.

+    chunk larger than the number of experts (8).

+    num_experts, hidden, inter, group = 5, 64, 32, 16
+

+        return torch.randint(

+        )
+
+    def block_scale(rows: int, cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        scale = torch.rand(num_experts, rows, cols // group, device=device) * 4 + 0.5
+        return scale.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+    w13_packed, w13_scale = packed(2 * inter, hidden), block_scale(2 * inter, hidden)

+    w2_global = torch.rand(num_experts, device=device) + 0.5

+        # compatibility checks require every projection to share it.

 - `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`: Timeout (in seconds) for automatically releasing the prefiller’s KV cache for a particular request. (Optional)
     - Default: 480
     - If a request is aborted and the decoder has not yet notified the prefiller, the prefill instance will release its KV-cache blocks after this timeout to avoid holding them indefinitely.

 ## KV Transfer Config
 
@@ -80,6 +81,10 @@ cache), see [ECMooncakeConnector Usage Guide](mooncake_ec_connector_usage.md).
 - **num_workers**: Size of thread pool for one prefiller worker to transfer KV caches by mooncake. (default 10)
 - **mooncake_protocol**: Mooncake connector protocol. (default "rdma")
 - **device_name**: Comma-separated whitelist of RDMA devices (e.g. `"mlx5_0,mlx5_1"`) to restrict topology discovery to. Empty discovers every device. Useful on hosts exposing a mix of InfiniBand and RoCE ports, where both peers must settle on the same link layer.
+- **kv_lease_duration**: Seconds the prefiller holds a finished request's KV blocks before the decoder must renew them. (default unset)
+    - Unset keeps the fixed `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.
+    - When set, the decoder renews the lease every `kv_lease_duration / 6` seconds from the time the request arrives until its pull settles, and each renewal extends it to at least `kv_lease_duration * 2 / 3` seconds from then, as in [NixlConnector](../design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md). Blocks of a decoder that crashed are freed within about `kv_lease_duration` seconds, while requests queued on a busy decoder keep their blocks.
+    - Set the same value on prefill and decode instances. A decoder without it does not renew, so its requests that wait longer than the lease lose their prefilled KV; a prefiller without it rejects renewals, and the decoder logs a warning. Prefill instances from releases without this option log an error for each renewal they receive, so upgrade them before enabling it on decode instances.
 - **bootstrap_server_address**: Optional `"host:port"` of an already running Mooncake bootstrap server. All prefiller ranks register with this endpoint instead of launching an embedded server. The caller owns the server lifetime and must configure the proxy to use the same endpoint. The example proxy assumes the bootstrap server is on the prefiller API host; a different host requires a proxy that supplies that address in `remote_bootstrap_addr`. Omit this option to use the embedded server and `VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT`.

+def _build_nan_route(rs):
+    """stage_route then load_route, then a flat load of each ordered pick.
+
+    The draft's all-NaN scores pick one expert twice. load_route counts picks
+    with a token bitmap, so the order table is short and the unread entries stay
+    at the sentinel. The flat load of that index is the gather that faults."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.common.sync import Addr, Mailbox, Space
+
+    words = rs.tab_words
+    tokens, topk = rs.tokens, rs.topk
+    n = tokens * topk

+    @fx.struct
+    class Lds:
+        tab: fx.Array[fx.Int32, words, 16]
+        red: fx.Array[fx.Float32, 16, 16]
+
+    @fx.union
+    class U:
+        t: Lds
+
+    @flyc.kernel(
+        name=f"test_nan_route_{tokens}_{topk}", known_block_size=[THREADS, 1, 1]
+    )
+    def kern(logit: Int64, bias: Int64, route: Int64, x: Int64, ids: Int64):
+        tid = fx.thread_idx.x
+        lds = fx.SharedAllocator().allocate(U).t.peek()
+        for i in range_constexpr(-(-words // THREADS)):
+            u = tid + THREADS * i
+            if u < words:
+                fx.ptr_store(fx.Int32(0x7FFFFFFF), lds.tab.ptr + u)
+        gpu.barrier()
+        mb = Mailbox(fx.Int32(1))
+        c = {

+            "args": {"bias": bias},
+            "put": mb.put,
+            "poll": mb.poll,
+            "logit": Addr("logit", Space.SCRATCH, logit),
+            "route": Addr("route", Space.SCRATCH, route),
+        }
+        for t in range_constexpr(tokens):
+            M.stage_route(c, t)
+        gpu.barrier()
+        M.load_route(c, lds.tab.ptr)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Engram host tables in host-NUMA cuMem, shared across DP ranks by FABRIC handle.
+
+GPUs map cuMem host memory with 2M pages instead of the 64K pages of a registered
+/dev/shm mapping, so random row lookups miss the TLB far less.
+"""
+
+import ctypes
+import weakref
+from functools import cache
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cu
+
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import GroupCoordinator
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.engram import describe_error, gather_errors
+from vllm.utils.cpu_resource_utils import get_memory_node_info
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+FABRIC_HANDLE = cu.CUmemAllocationHandleType.CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC
+# Tables are created in chunks, so the creator can stop before draining its node.
+CHUNK_BYTES = 2 << 30
+# Fraction of the NUMA node left to other allocations.
+NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION = 0.05
+
+
+class ExportedHostTable(NamedTuple):
+    """What a peer needs to map a table."""
+
+    numa_node: int
+    padded_bytes: int
+    fabric_handles: list[bytes]
+
+
+def _chunk_ranges(padded_bytes: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    return [
+        (offset, min(CHUNK_BYTES, padded_bytes - offset))
+        for offset in range(0, padded_bytes, CHUNK_BYTES)
+    ]
+
+
+def _call_driver(fn, *args):
+    """Call a CUDA driver API and return its result, raising on failure."""
+    error, *result = fn(*args)
+    if error != cu.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{fn.__name__} failed: {error.name}")
+    return result[0] if result else None
+
+
+def _gpu_numa_node() -> int:
+    return _call_driver(
+        cu.cuDeviceGetAttribute,
+        cu.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID,
+        torch.accelerator.current_device_index(),
+    )
+
+
+def _host_allocation_prop(numa_node: int) -> cu.CUmemAllocationProp:
+    prop = cu.CUmemAllocationProp()
+    prop.type = cu.CUmemAllocationType.CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED
+    prop.location.type = cu.CUmemLocationType.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA
+    prop.location.id = numa_node
+    prop.requestedHandleTypes = FABRIC_HANDLE
+    return prop
+
+
+def _allocation_granularity(prop: cu.CUmemAllocationProp) -> int:
+    return _call_driver(cu.cuMemGetAllocationGranularity, prop, 0)
+
+
+def _export_fabric_handle(handle) -> bytes:
+    exported = _call_driver(cu.cuMemExportToShareableHandle, handle, FABRIC_HANDLE, 0)
+    return bytes(exported.data)
+
+
+def _release(handles: list) -> None:
+    for handle in handles:
+        cu.cuMemRelease(handle)
+
+
+def _read_write_access(location_type, location_id: int) -> cu.CUmemAccessDesc:
+    access = cu.CUmemAccessDesc()
+    access.location.type = location_type
+    access.location.id = location_id
+    access.flags = cu.CUmemAccess_flags.CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READWRITE
+    return access
+
+
+def _unmap(address: int, size: int, ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> None:
+    for offset, length in ranges:
+        cu.cuMemUnmap(address + offset, length)
+    cu.cuMemAddressFree(address, size)
+
+
+@cache
+def fabric_host_memory_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether host-NUMA cuMem allocations can export FABRIC handles here."""
+    try:
+        prop = _host_allocation_prop(_gpu_numa_node())
+        handle = _call_driver(cu.cuMemCreate, _allocation_granularity(prop), prop, 0)
+        try:
+            _export_fabric_handle(handle)
+        finally:
+            cu.cuMemRelease(handle)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Host-NUMA cuMem FABRIC handles are unavailable (%s); Engram DP "
+            "replicas share tables through /dev/shm.",
+            exc,
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+

+def _create_table(num_bytes: int) -> tuple[list, ExportedHostTable]:
+    """Allocate and export a table on this GPU's host NUMA node.
+
+    Stops once the node would drop below its reserve. The kernel compacts to
+    find 2M pages and fails the chunk, rather than OOM-killing, if it cannot.
+    """
+    numa_node = _gpu_numa_node()
+    prop = _host_allocation_prop(numa_node)
+    padded_bytes = round_up(num_bytes, _allocation_granularity(prop))
+    reserve = get_memory_node_info(numa_node).total_memory * NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION
+    handles: list = []
+    try:
+        for offset, length in _chunk_ranges(padded_bytes):
+            handles.append(_call_driver(cu.cuMemCreate, length, prop, 0))
+            if get_memory_node_info(numa_node).available_memory < reserve:
+                raise MemoryError(
+                    f"NUMA node {numa_node} fell below its "
+                    f"{reserve / 2**30:.1f} GiB reserve after "
+                    f"{(offset + length) / 2**30:.1f} of "
+                    f"{padded_bytes / 2**30:.1f} GiB"
+                )
+        exported = [_export_fabric_handle(handle) for handle in handles]
+    except BaseException:
+        _release(handles)
+        raise

+                    )
+                )
+        address = int(_call_driver(cu.cuMemAddressReserve, table.padded_bytes, 0, 0, 0))
+        for (offset, length), handle in zip(_chunk_ranges(table.padded_bytes), handles):
+            _call_driver(cu.cuMemMap, address + offset, length, 0, handle, 0)
+            mapped.append((offset, length))
+        location = cu.CUmemLocationType
+        access = [
+            _read_write_access(location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE, device),
+            _read_write_access(
+                location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA, table.numa_node
+            ),
+        ]
+        _call_driver(
+            cu.cuMemSetAccess, address, table.padded_bytes, access, len(access)
+        )
+    except BaseException:
+        if address is not None:
+            _unmap(address, table.padded_bytes, mapped)
+        raise
+    finally:
+        # The mappings keep the allocations alive.
+        _release(handles)
+
+    host_buffer = (ctypes.c_uint8 * num_bytes).from_address(address)
+    finalizer = weakref.finalize(
+        host_buffer, _unmap, address, table.padded_bytes, mapped
+    )
+    finalizer.atexit = False  # type: ignore[misc]
+    # Torch retains this object, so the GPU view keeps the buffer alive too.
+    # Name the device: an index-less "cuda" makes torch copy the table.
+    gpu_view = torch.as_tensor(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            __cuda_array_interface__={
+                "shape": (num_bytes,),
+                "typestr": "|u1",
+                "data": (address, False),
+                "version": 3,
+            },
+            owner=host_buffer,
+        ),
+        device=torch.device("cuda", device),
+    )

+    num_bytes: int, group: GroupCoordinator

+    """Map one table on every rank of a node-local group, or None on all of them.
+
+    Rank 0 creates the table and broadcasts its handles; the others import them.
+    Returns CPU and GPU uint8 views of the table.
+    """
+    handles: list = []
+    table = error = None
+    if group.rank_in_group == 0 and fabric_host_memory_supported():
+        try:
+            handles, table = _create_table(num_bytes)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            error = describe_error(exc)
+    table, error = group.broadcast_object((table, error))
+    if table is not None:
+        views = None
+        try:
+            views = _map_table(table, num_bytes, handles)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            error = describe_error(exc)
+        if not (error := gather_errors(group, error)):
+            return views
+    if error and group.rank_in_group == 0:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Engram host table cannot use host-NUMA cuMem (%s); falling back "
+            "to /dev/shm, whose 64K GPU pages make lookups slower.",
+            error,
+        )
+    return None

+def _flydsl_kernel_symbols(module: object, infer_kernel_names) -> str | None:
+    """Name the ``gpu.func`` kernels in a module about to be compiled.
+
+    ``func_name`` is the Python launcher name, which many kernels share
+    verbatim (``launch``), so the ``gpu.func`` symbols are what identify the
+    kernel and the width that needs warmup.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""EPLB replica mapping and expert-load recording shared by Triton kernels."""
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def eplb_map_and_record(
+    logical_ids,
+    token_idx,
+    mask,
+    logical_to_physical,
+    replica_count,
+    num_logical,
+    map_stride,
+    expert_load,
+    num_physical,
+    record_enabled,
+    num_unpadded_tokens,
+):
+    """Map logical expert ids to physical replicas and record expert load.
+
+    ``token_idx`` broadcasts against ``logical_ids``; masked-off or
+    out-of-range ids map to -1.
+    """
+    valid = mask & (logical_ids >= 0) & (logical_ids < num_logical)
+    safe_ids = tl.where(valid, logical_ids, 0)
+    replicas = tl.load(replica_count + safe_ids, mask=valid, other=1)
+    # floor(2^32 / phi), classic Knuth multiplicative hash multiplier.
+    KNUTH_MULTIPLIER = 2654435769
+    hashed = (token_idx.to(tl.int64) * KNUTH_MULTIPLIER) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    physical_ids = tl.load(
+        logical_to_physical + safe_ids * map_stride + hashed % replicas,
+        mask=valid,
+        other=-1,
+    )
+
+    record = (
+        (tl.load(record_enabled) != 0)
+        & (physical_ids >= 0)
+        & (physical_ids < num_physical)
+    )
+    if num_unpadded_tokens is not None:
+        record &= token_idx < tl.load(num_unpadded_tokens)
+    tl.atomic_add(expert_load + tl.where(record, physical_ids, 0), 1, mask=record)
+    return physical_ids

[Doc] Add k8s-aibom to deployment integrations (#60899)

Signed-off-by: Glen Messenger <57537684+glenmessenger@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

new file mode 100644
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+# k8s-aibom
+
+[k8s-aibom](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-aibom) is an open-source Kubernetes controller that keeps an inventory of the AI workloads actually serving in a cluster. For every vLLM deployment it produces a [CycloneDX ML-BOM](https://cyclonedx.org/capabilities/mlbom/): the vLLM image and resolved digest, the model the server was started with, and, when the model is signed, the verified signer identity. Each attribute carries the evidence it was read from and a confidence tier (declared, inferred, or unresolved).
+
+It is read-only toward your cluster: it watches workloads through the Kubernetes API, adds no sidecars or init containers, runs unprivileged, and never changes scheduling or serving behavior. vLLM is detected whether you run it as a plain Deployment or StatefulSet, as a LeaderWorkerSet or DisaggregatedSet, under [KubeAI](kubeai.md), [KServe](kserve.md), [KubeRay](kuberay.md), [llm-d](llm-d.md), or the [production stack](production-stack.md), which ships it as an optional chart dependency.
+
+## Install
+
+```bash
+helm install k8s-aibom oci://ghcr.io/googlecloudplatform/charts/k8s-aibom \
+  --version 1.6.0 \
+  --namespace k8s-aibom-system --create-namespace
+```
+
+Then opt in each namespace that serves models:
+
+```bash
+kubectl label namespace <your-serving-namespace> aibom.k8saibom.dev/enabled=true
+```
+
+Documents appear as `AIBOM` resources next to the workloads they describe. The `kubectl aibom` plugin (`kubectl krew install aibom`) summarizes and searches them:
+
+```bash
+kubectl aibom summary -A
+kubectl aibom find --runtime vllm -A
+kubectl aibom find --image vllm/vllm-openai -A
+```
+
+See the [k8s-aibom documentation](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-aibom#readme) for the document format, signature verification, external sinks, and the full list of detected runtimes.

-class OlmoeMoE(nn.Module):
-    """A tensor-parallel MoE implementation for Olmoe that shards each expert
-    across all ranks.

-    Each expert's weights are sharded across all ranks and a fused MoE
-    kernel is used for the forward pass, and finally we reduce the outputs
-    across ranks.
-    """

-    def __init__(
-        self,
-        num_experts: int,
-        top_k: int,
-        hidden_size: int,
-        intermediate_size: int,
-        params_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
-        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
-        tp_size: int | None = None,
-        prefix: str = "",

-        super().__init__()

-        self.gate = GateLinear(
-            hidden_size,
-            num_experts,
-            prefix=f"{prefix}.gate",
-        )
-
-        self.experts = FusedMoEFactory(
-            num_experts=num_experts,
-            top_k=top_k,
-            hidden_size=hidden_size,
-            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
-            renormalize=False,
-            quant_config=quant_config,
-            tp_size=tp_size,
-            prefix=f"{prefix}.experts",
-        )

-    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

-        hidden_states = hidden_states.view(-1, hidden_dim)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""pytest plugin for AMD CI jobs: leave without native teardown once pytest is done.
+
+A pytest process can crash in native library destructors after its summary:
+vllm/ci #96786 printed "236 passed" and then died with SIGSEGV (exit 139) during
+interpreter shutdown, past the point where faulthandler reports. Once the outermost
+session has finished, this runs the Python exit handlers (engine shutdown, Ray,
+multiprocessing cleanup), flushes, and exits with pytest's own status, skipping
+module teardown and native destructors. pytest's result is never changed, and a
+command chain still stops on a real failure.
+
+Off when a kernel recorder is loaded (it writes its trace during native teardown)
+or with VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT=0.
+"""
+
+import atexit
+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+_outer = None
+_session = None
+
+
+def _recorder_loaded() -> bool:
+    return bool(
+        os.environ.get("ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES")
+        or os.environ.get("CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH")
+        or "rocprofiler" in os.environ.get("LD_PRELOAD", "")
+    )
+
+
+def pytest_configure(config):
+    global _outer
+    if _outer is None:  # pytester runs nested sessions in-process; act on the outer one
+        _outer = config
+
+
+def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
+    global _session
+    if session.config is _outer:
+        _session = session
+
+
+@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)
+def pytest_unconfigure(config):
+    if config is not _outer or _session is None:
+        return
+    if os.environ.get("VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT") == "0" or _recorder_loaded():
+        return
+    status = int(_session.exitstatus)
+    sys.stdout.flush()
+    sys.stderr.flush()
+    try:
+        atexit._run_exitfuncs()
+    except BaseException as exc:  # an exit handler failing must not mask the result
+        print(f"[amd-ci] exit handler failed: {exc!r}", file=sys.stderr)
+    print(
+        f"[amd-ci] pytest finished with exit {status}; leaving without native teardown",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    sys.stdout.flush()
+    os._exit(status)

-###############################################################################
-# Pytest marker/keyword re-quoting
-#
-# When commands are passed through Buildkite -> shell -> $* -> bash -c,
-# quotes around multi-word pytest -m/-k expressions get stripped:
-#   pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' v1/core
-# becomes:
-#   pytest -v -s -m not cpu_test v1/core
-#
-# pytest then interprets "cpu_test" as a file path, not part of the marker.
-#
-# This function detects unquoted expressions after -m/-k and re-quotes them
-# by collecting tokens until a recognizable boundary is reached:
-#   - test path (contains '/')
-#   - test file (ends with '.py')
-#   - another pytest flag (--xxx or -x single-char flags)
-#   - command separator (&& || ; |)
-#   - environment variable assignment (FOO=bar)
-#
-# Single-word markers (e.g. -m cpu_test, -m hybrid_model) pass through
-# unquoted since they have no spaces and work fine.
-#
-# Already-quoted expressions (containing literal single quotes) are passed
-# through untouched to avoid double-quoting well-formed shell fragments.
-#
-# NOTE: This ONLY fixes -m/-k flags. It cannot recover arbitrary inner
-# double-quotes stripped by the calling shell (see header comment).
-# Use VLLM_TEST_COMMANDS to avoid the problem entirely.
-###############################################################################
-re_quote_pytest_markers() {
-  local input="$1"
-  local output=""
-  local collecting=false
-  local marker_buf=""
-
-  # Strip backslash-newline continuations, then flatten remaining newlines
-  local flat="${input//$'\\\n'/ }"
-  flat="${flat//$'\n'/ }"
-
-  # Disable globbing to prevent *.py etc. from expanding during read -ra
-  local restore_glob
-  restore_glob="$(shopt -p -o noglob 2>/dev/null || true)"
-  set -o noglob
-  local -a words
-  read -ra words <<< "$flat"
-  eval "$restore_glob"
-
-  for word in "${words[@]}"; do
-    if $collecting; then
-      # If the token we're about to collect already contains a literal
-      # single quote, the expression was already quoted upstream.
-      # Flush and stop collecting.
-      if [[ "$word" == *"'"* ]]; then
-        if [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-          # Should not normally happen (partial buf + quote), flush raw
-          output+="${marker_buf} "
-          marker_buf=""
-        fi
-        output+="${word} "
-        collecting=false
-        continue
-      fi
-
-      local is_boundary=false
-      case "$word" in
-        # Line-continuation artifact
-        "\\")
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Command separators
-        "&&"|"||"|";"|"|")
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Long flags (--ignore, --shard-id, etc.)
-        --*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Short flags (-v, -s, -x, etc.) but NOT negative marker tokens
-        # like "not" which don't start with "-". Also skip -k/-m which
-        # would start a new marker (handled below).
-        -[a-zA-Z])
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Test path (contains /)
-        */*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Test file (ends with .py, possibly with ::method)
-        *.py|*.py::*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Environment variable assignment preceding a command (FOO=bar)
-        *=*)
-          # Only treat as boundary if it looks like VAR=value, not
-          # pytest filter expressions like num_gpus=2 inside markers
-          if [[ "$word" =~ ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*= ]]; then
-            is_boundary=true
-          fi
-          ;;
-      esac
-
-      if $is_boundary; then
-        # Strip surrounding double quotes if present (from upstream
-        # single-to-double conversion); without this, wrapping below
-        # would produce '"expr"' with literal double-quote characters.
-        if [[ "$marker_buf" == '"'*'"' ]]; then
-          marker_buf="${marker_buf#\"}"
-          marker_buf="${marker_buf%\"}"
-        fi
-        # Flush the collected marker expression
-        if [[ "$marker_buf" == *" "* || "$marker_buf" == *"("* ]]; then
-          output+="'${marker_buf}' "
-        else
-          output+="${marker_buf} "
-        fi
-        collecting=false
-        marker_buf=""
-        # Check if this boundary word itself starts a new -m/-k
-        if [[ "$word" == "-m" || "$word" == "-k" ]]; then
-          output+="${word} "
-          collecting=true
-        # Drop stray backslash tokens silently
-        elif [[ "$word" == "\\" ]]; then
-          :
-        else
-          output+="${word} "
-        fi
-      else
-        # Accumulate into marker buffer
-        if [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-          marker_buf+=" ${word}"
-        else
-          marker_buf="${word}"
-        fi
-      fi
-    elif [[ "$word" == "-m" || "$word" == "-k" ]]; then
-      output+="${word} "
-      collecting=true
-      marker_buf=""
-    else
-      output+="${word} "
-    fi
-  done
-
-  # Flush any trailing marker expression (marker at end of command)
-  if $collecting && [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-    # Strip surrounding double quotes (see mid-stream flush comment)
-    if [[ "$marker_buf" == '"'*'"' ]]; then
-      marker_buf="${marker_buf#\"}"
-      marker_buf="${marker_buf%\"}"
-    fi
-    if [[ "$marker_buf" == *" "* || "$marker_buf" == *"("* ]]; then
-      output+="'${marker_buf}'"
-    else
-      output+="${marker_buf}"
-    fi
-  fi
-
-  echo "${output% }"
-}

+# Promote ROCm release artifacts without rebuilding anything.
+# The release pipeline's build step (build.sh release) pushed the source images to

+#

+#            With NIGHTLY=1, also push the nightly tags to Docker Hub.
+#

+#   BUILDKITE_COMMIT   — the commit being released
+#   ECR            — ECR repository prefix (release-pipeline.yaml's ROCM_CI_REPO)
+#
+# Optional:
+#   HUB            — Docker Hub repo for nightly images (default: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm)
+#   NIGHTLY        — set to 1 to push nightly Hub tags (default: 0)
+#   DOCKERHUB_USERNAME — Hub username for cleanup script (default: vllmbot)
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Arguments
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+STACK=$1
+MODE=$2
+COMMIT=${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:?BUILDKITE_COMMIT must be set}
+
+ECR=${ECR:?ECR must be set (by release-pipeline.yaml)}

+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helper functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# retry <cmd...>  — registry lookups: these steps have no retry rules
+retry() { "$@" || { sleep 5; "$@"; } || { sleep 5; "$@"; }; }

+# pin <ref>  — resolve <ref> to a pinned ref@digest (resolves once, stable for the rest of the script).
+#   Parses the validated "Digest:" line, as build.sh does.
+pin() {
+  local d
+  d=$(retry docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" | awk '$1 == "Digest:" { print $2; exit }')
+  [[ $d =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { echo "cannot resolve the digest of $1" >&2; return 1; }
+  echo "$1@$d"
+}

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-ARG USE_SCCACHE
-ARG SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL
-ARG SCCACHE_ENDPOINT
-ARG SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME=vllm-build-sccache
-ARG SCCACHE_REGION_NAME=us-west-2
-ARG SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS=0
-
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS base
-
-ARG ARG_PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH
-ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=${ARG_PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH:-${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}}
-
-# Install build dependencies and utilities
-RUN apt-get update -q -y && apt-get install -q -y \
-    sqlite3 libsqlite3-dev libfmt-dev libmsgpack-dev libsuitesparse-dev \
-    apt-transport-https ca-certificates wget curl \
-    libnuma-dev ccache mold
-RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
-    python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
-# Note: mold is installed but not set as the system default linker because
-# some packages use JIT compilation at runtime with flags mold does not support.
-# Build stages opt in via LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold".
-# Remove sccache only if not using sccache (it exists in base image from Dockerfile.rocm_72_base)
-ARG USE_SCCACHE
-RUN if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" != "1" ]; then \
-        apt-get purge -y sccache || true; \
-        python3 -m pip uninstall -y sccache || true; \
-        rm -f "$(which sccache)" || true; \
-    fi
-
-# Install UV — download first, then run, so a curl failure is not masked by the pipe
-RUN curl -LsSf --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh -o /tmp/uv-install.sh \
-    && env UV_INSTALL_DIR="/usr/local/bin" sh /tmp/uv-install.sh \
-    && rm -f /tmp/uv-install.sh \
-    && uv --version
-
-# This timeout (in seconds) is necessary when installing some dependencies via uv since it's likely to time out
-# Reference: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/1694
-ENV UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=500
-ENV UV_INDEX_STRATEGY="unsafe-best-match"
-# Use copy mode to avoid hardlink failures with Docker cache mounts
-ENV UV_LINK_MODE=copy
-# ccache directory - persisted across layer rebuilds via cache mounts.
-ENV CCACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/ccache
-ENV CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK=content
-# Empty by default so build steps fall back to $(nproc); CI can override.
-ARG max_jobs
-ENV MAX_JOBS=${max_jobs}
-
-# Install sccache if USE_SCCACHE is enabled (for release builds)
-ARG USE_SCCACHE
-ARG SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL
-ARG SCCACHE_ENDPOINT
-ARG SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME
-ARG SCCACHE_REGION_NAME
-ARG SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS
-RUN if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
-        if command -v sccache >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
-            echo "sccache already installed, skipping installation"; \
-            sccache --version; \
-        else \
-            echo "Installing sccache..." \
-            && SCCACHE_ARCH="x86_64" \
-            && SCCACHE_VERSION="v0.8.1" \
-            && SCCACHE_DL_URL="${SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL:-https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases/download/${SCCACHE_VERSION}/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz}" \
-            && curl -L -o /tmp/sccache.tar.gz ${SCCACHE_DL_URL} \
-            && tar -xzf /tmp/sccache.tar.gz -C /tmp \
-            && mv /tmp/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl/sccache /usr/bin/sccache \
-            && chmod +x /usr/bin/sccache \
-            && rm -rf /tmp/sccache.tar.gz /tmp/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl \
-            && sccache --version; \
-        fi; \
-    fi
-
-# Set sccache environment variables only when USE_SCCACHE=1
-# This prevents S3 config from leaking into images when sccache is not used
-ARG USE_SCCACHE
-ENV SCCACHE_BUCKET=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME}}
-ENV SCCACHE_REGION=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_REGION_NAME}}
-ENV SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS}}
-ENV SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=${USE_SCCACHE:+0}
-
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-WORKDIR ${COMMON_WORKDIR}
-
-
-# -----------------------
-# vLLM fetch stages
-FROM base AS fetch_vllm_0
-ONBUILD COPY ./ vllm/
-FROM base AS fetch_vllm_1
-ARG VLLM_REPO
-ARG VLLM_BRANCH
-ONBUILD RUN git clone ${VLLM_REPO} \
-	    && cd vllm \
-	    && git fetch -v --prune -- origin ${VLLM_BRANCH} \
-	    && git checkout FETCH_HEAD \
-        && if [ ${VLLM_REPO} != "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git" ] ; then \
-               git remote add upstream "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git" \
-               && git fetch upstream ; fi
-FROM fetch_vllm_${REMOTE_VLLM} AS fetch_vllm
-
-# Resolve the device-independent source version once for every downstream
-# artifact. setuptools-scm reads Git metadata for local/remote sources and the
-# archive metadata generated for canonical CI contexts.
-FROM fetch_vllm AS vllm-version
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-RUN --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-uv,target=/root/.cache/uv \
-    cd ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm \
-    && uv pip install --system -r requirements/build/rust.txt \
-    && python3 -c \
-        "from setuptools_scm import get_version; print(get_version(git_describe_command=['git', 'describe', '--dirty', '--tags', '--long', '--abbrev=40', '--match', 'v[0-9]*']))" \
-        > /vllm-version.txt
-
-# -----------------------
-# Rust toolchain inputs
-#
-# Keep these separate from Rust source inputs so Rust source-only changes do not
-# invalidate the long-lived ci_base image that carries the toolchain.
-FROM scratch AS rust_toolchain_input_0
-COPY rust-toolchain.toml /rust-toolchain-input/vllm/rust-toolchain.toml
-
-FROM base AS rust_toolchain_input_1
-ARG VLLM_REPO
-ARG VLLM_BRANCH
-RUN git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none ${VLLM_REPO} /rust-toolchain-input/vllm \
-    && cd /rust-toolchain-input/vllm \
-    && git fetch -v --prune -- origin ${VLLM_BRANCH} \
-    && git sparse-checkout init --no-cone \
-    && git sparse-checkout set \
-        rust-toolchain.toml \
-    && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
-
-FROM rust_toolchain_input_${REMOTE_VLLM} AS rust-toolchain-input
-
-# -----------------------
-# Rust build inputs
-#
-# REMOTE_VLLM=0: use only the local files that can affect Rust artifacts.
-# REMOTE_VLLM=1: fetch only those same files from the requested remote ref.
-FROM scratch AS rust_input_0
-COPY requirements/build/rust.txt /rust-input/vllm/requirements/build/rust.txt
-COPY rust/Cargo.lock rust/Cargo.toml /rust-input/vllm/rust/
-COPY rust/proto /rust-input/vllm/rust/proto
-COPY rust/src /rust-input/vllm/rust/src
-COPY rust-toolchain.toml /rust-input/vllm/rust-toolchain.toml
-COPY tools/build_rust.py /rust-input/vllm/tools/build_rust.py
-COPY tools/build_rust.sh /rust-input/vllm/tools/build_rust.sh
-
-FROM base AS rust_input_1
-ARG VLLM_REPO
-ARG VLLM_BRANCH
-RUN git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none ${VLLM_REPO} /rust-input/vllm \
-    && cd /rust-input/vllm \
-    && git fetch -v --prune -- origin ${VLLM_BRANCH} \
-    && git sparse-checkout init --no-cone \
-    && git sparse-checkout set \
-        requirements/build/rust.txt \
-        rust/Cargo.lock \
-        rust/Cargo.toml \
-        rust/proto/** \
-        rust/src/** \
-        rust-toolchain.toml \
-        tools/build_rust.py \
-        tools/build_rust.sh \
-    && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
-
-FROM rust_input_${REMOTE_VLLM} AS rust-input
-
-# -----------------------
-# Rust toolchain
-FROM base AS rust-toolchain
-
-ENV CARGO_HOME=/root/.cargo
-ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/root/.rustup
-ENV PATH=${CARGO_HOME}/bin:${PATH}
-
-RUN apt-get update -q -y && apt-get install -q -y --no-install-recommends \
-        ca-certificates curl \
-    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
-
-COPY --from=rust-toolchain-input /rust-toolchain-input/vllm/rust-toolchain.toml /tmp/rust-toolchain.toml
-RUN TOOLCHAIN="$(grep '^channel' /tmp/rust-toolchain.toml | sed 's/.*= *"\(.*\)"/\1/')" \
-    && if ! command -v rustup >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
-        curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs \
-            | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none; \
-    fi \
-    && rustup toolchain install "${TOOLCHAIN}" \
-    && rustup default "${TOOLCHAIN}" \
-    && rustc --version \
-    && cargo --version
-
-# -----------------------
-# Rust build stage
-# Builds the `vllm-rs` frontend in a dedicated stage so the wheel build stages
-# don't need the rust toolchain.
-FROM rust-toolchain AS rust-build
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-ARG USE_SCCACHE
-
-# Cap cargo parallelism to avoid exhausting the AMD CI host's open-file limit
-# (rustc spawns enough concurrent processes to hit RLIMIT_NOFILE otherwise).
-ENV CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4
-ENV CARGO_NET_RETRY=10
-ENV RUSTUP_MAX_RETRIES=10
-
-WORKDIR ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm
-
-COPY --from=rust-input /rust-input/vllm/requirements/build/rust.txt requirements/build/rust.txt
-
-# BuildKit can run this stage in parallel with ROCm native builds. Keep Rust on
-# a separate local sccache daemon while sharing the same remote cache backend.
-ENV SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT=4227
-
-RUN --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-uv,target=/root/.cache/uv \
-    uv pip install --system -r requirements/build/rust.txt
-
-COPY --from=rust-input /rust-input/vllm/rust rust
-COPY --from=rust-input /rust-input/vllm/rust-toolchain.toml rust-toolchain.toml
-COPY --from=rust-input /rust-input/vllm/tools/build_rust.py tools/build_rust.py
-COPY --from=rust-input /rust-input/vllm/tools/build_rust.sh tools/build_rust.sh
-COPY --from=vllm-version /vllm-version.txt /tmp/vllm-version.txt
-
-# Build the release binary. Cargo's registry/git caches can be written by
-# concurrent BuildKit jobs on shared workers, so lock those cache mounts while
-# keeping the cache benefit. Do not cache target/, because stale target metadata
-# can outlive source updates across BuildKit cache reuse.
-RUN --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-cargo-registry,target=/root/.cargo/registry,sharing=locked \
-    --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-cargo-git,target=/root/.cargo/git,sharing=locked \
-    if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
-        export RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache \
-        && sccache --show-stats; \
-    fi \
-    && export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION="$(cat /tmp/vllm-version.txt)" \
-    && bash tools/build_rust.sh \
-    && test -x vllm/vllm-rs \
-    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
-        sccache --show-stats; \
-    fi
-
-# -----------------------
-# Shared vLLM build dependencies
-#
-# Install requirements once, before bringing source-specific inputs into either
-# consumer. Native compilation and wheel packaging then share this expensive
-# layer while retaining their independent source cache boundaries.
-FROM base AS build_vllm_dependencies
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
-WORKDIR ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm
-
-COPY --from=fetch_vllm \
-    ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/requirements/common.txt \
-    ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/requirements/rocm.txt \
-    requirements/
-
-RUN --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-uv,target=/root/.cache/uv \
-    uv pip install --system -r requirements/rocm.txt
-
-# Fetch only the pinned ROCm Triton kernels package. Keeping this before the
-# vLLM source COPYs makes the download reusable when native sources change.
-FROM base AS rocm-triton-kernels
-ARG ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT
-ADD https://codeload.github.com/ROCm/triton/tar.gz/${ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT} \
-    /tmp/rocm-triton.tar.gz
-RUN mkdir -p /opt/rocm-triton-kernels \
-    && tar --extract --gzip --file /tmp/rocm-triton.tar.gz \
-        --directory /opt/rocm-triton-kernels --strip-components=4 \
-        --no-same-owner \
-        "triton-${ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT}/python/triton_kernels/triton_kernels" \
-    && test -f /opt/rocm-triton-kernels/__init__.py \
-    && rm /tmp/rocm-triton.tar.gz
-
-# -----------------------
-# vLLM native build stages
-#
-# csrc-build intentionally copies only files that affect ROCm native extension
-# compilation. That keeps unrelated CI/test/docs edits from invalidating the
-# expensive HIP/C++ build layer.
-FROM build_vllm_dependencies AS csrc-build
-ARG ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT
-COPY --from=rocm-triton-kernels \
-    /opt/rocm-triton-kernels /opt/rocm-triton-kernels
-ENV TRITON_KERNELS_SRC_DIR=/opt/rocm-triton-kernels
-
-# pyproject.toml is bind-mounted so it is not persisted in the csrc-build image,
-# but it still participates in the BuildKit cache key for this RUN step.
-COPY setup.py CMakeLists.txt ./
-COPY tools/build_rust.py tools/build_rust.py
-COPY cmake cmake/
-COPY csrc csrc/
-COPY vllm/envs.py vllm/envs.py
-COPY vllm/__init__.py vllm/__init__.py
-
-ENV SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION="0.0.0+rocm.csrc.build"
-
-RUN --mount=type=bind,source=pyproject.toml,target=${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/pyproject.toml \
-    --mount=type=cache,id=vllm-rocm-ccache,target=/root/.cache/ccache \
-    grep -Fq "set(TRITON_KERNELS_TAG \"${ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT}\")" \
-        cmake/external_projects/triton_kernels.cmake \
-    && export CCACHE_BASEDIR="$PWD" \
-    && echo "=== ccache stats before ROCm native build ===" \
-    && (ccache --show-stats || true) \
-    && (ccache --zero-stats || true) \
-    && EFFECTIVE_MAX_JOBS="${MAX_JOBS:-$(nproc)}" \
-    && echo "Building ROCm native extension wheel with MAX_JOBS=${EFFECTIVE_MAX_JOBS}" \
-    && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" MAX_JOBS="${EFFECTIVE_MAX_JOBS}" python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
-    && test -d dist \
-    && ls dist/*.whl >/dev/null \
-    && echo "=== ccache stats after ROCm native build ===" \
-    && (ccache --show-stats || true)
-
-# Build the full vLLM ROCm wheel by reusing the native extension wheel from
-# csrc-build. This stage still rebuilds for Python/package changes, but skips
-# the expensive dependency installation and HIP/C++ compilation when their
-# respective inputs are unchanged.
-FROM build_vllm_dependencies AS build_vllm
-COPY --from=fetch_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm
-COPY --from=csrc-build ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/dist /precompiled-wheels
-COPY --from=vllm-version /vllm-version.txt /tmp/vllm-version.txt
-
-# Drop the pre-built Rust artifacts into the source tree. setup.py detects
-# them and ships them as-is, skipping the local Rust build.
-COPY --from=rust-build ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/vllm-rs ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/vllm-rs
-COPY --from=rust-build ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/_rust_*.so ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/
-
-RUN cd "${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm" \
-    && export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION="$(cat /tmp/vllm-version.txt)" \
-    && export VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 \
-    && export VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_LOCATION="$(ls /precompiled-wheels/*.whl)" \
-    && export VLLM_DOCKER_BUILD_CONTEXT=1 \
-    && echo "Packaging vLLM ROCm wheel using precompiled extensions from ${VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_LOCATION}" \
-    && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
-    && test -d dist \
-    && ls dist/*.whl >/dev/null
-FROM scratch AS export_vllm
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/dist/*.whl /
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/requirements /requirements
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/benchmarks /benchmarks
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/tests /tests
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/examples /examples
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/tools /tools
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/Dockerfile /docker/Dockerfile
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/Dockerfile.cpu /docker/Dockerfile.cpu
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72 /docker/
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base /docker/
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/ci-rocm.hcl /docker/ci-rocm.hcl
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/docker-bake.hcl /docker/docker-bake.hcl
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl /docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/.buildkite /.buildkite
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/pyproject.toml /pyproject.toml
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/rust /rust
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/rust-toolchain.toml /rust-toolchain.toml
-COPY --from=build_vllm ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/v1 /vllm_v1
-
-# NIXL/UCX build stages
-FROM base AS build_nixl
-ARG NIXL_BRANCH="1683cf3b7f3d11674c03c5e861cea22339876c96"
-ARG NIXL_REPO="https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl.git"
-ARG UCX_BRANCH="2ff0b47ce7626584cb9b56c647d08f712c6c3edf"
-ARG UCX_REPO="https://github.com/openucx/ucx.git"
-ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm
-ENV UCX_HOME=/usr/local/ucx
-ENV NIXL_HOME=/usr/local/nixl
-
-# NIXL build system dependencies and RDMA support
-RUN apt-get -y update && apt-get -y install autoconf libtool pkg-config \
-    libgrpc-dev \
-    libgrpc++-dev \
-    libprotobuf-dev \
-    protobuf-compiler-grpc \
-    libcpprest-dev \
-    libaio-dev \
-    librdmacm1 \
-    librdmacm-dev \
-    libibverbs1 \
-    libibverbs-dev \
-    ibverbs-utils \
-    rdmacm-utils \
-    ibverbs-providers \
-    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
-
-RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
-    uv pip install --system meson meson-python pyyaml types-PyYAML \
-        auditwheel build patchelf pytest tomlkit "setuptools>=80.9.0"
-
-RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/ccache \
-    cd /usr/local/src && \
-    git clone ${UCX_REPO} &&  \
-    cd ucx  && \
-    git checkout ${UCX_BRANCH} && \
-    ./autogen.sh && \
-    mkdir build && cd build && \
-    CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++" \
-    ../configure \
-        --prefix=/usr/local/ucx \
-        --enable-shared \
-        --disable-static \
-        --disable-doxygen-doc \
-        --enable-optimizations \
-        --enable-devel-headers \
-        --with-rocm=${ROCM_PATH} \
-        --with-verbs \
-        --with-dm \
-        --enable-mt && \
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    make install
-
-ENV PATH=/usr/local/ucx/bin:$PATH
-ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${UCX_HOME}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
-
-RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/ccache \
-    git clone ${NIXL_REPO} /opt/nixl && \
-    cd /opt/nixl && \
-    git checkout ${NIXL_BRANCH} && \
-    CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++" \
-    meson setup build --prefix=${NIXL_HOME} \
-                     -Ducx_path=${UCX_HOME} \
-                     -Dwheel_variant=rocm \
-                     -Dbuild_tests=false \
-                     -Dbuild_examples=false && \
-    cd build && \
-    ninja -j$(nproc) && \
-    ninja install && \
-    echo "${NIXL_HOME}/lib/$(uname -m)-linux-gnu" \
-        > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/nixl.conf && \
-    echo "${NIXL_HOME}/lib/$(uname -m)-linux-gnu/plugins" \
-        >> /etc/ld.so.conf.d/nixl.conf && \
-    ldconfig
-
-# Generate the ROCm NIXL wheel. Upstream's generic wheel helper detects CUDA,
-# so configure the ROCm wheel variant directly through Meson.
-# Exclude libcore and libpull from auditwheel: transitive dependencies
-# that are not shipped in the wheel and vary across base images.
-# Tag manylinux_2_35 to match the Ubuntu 22.04 base: NIXL >= 1.5 links
-# GLIBCXX_3.4.30 symbols, which manylinux_2_34 does not allow.
-RUN cd /opt/nixl && \
-    ./contrib/tomlutil.py --wheel-name nixl-rocm pyproject.toml && \
-    CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++" \
-    uv build --wheel --no-build-isolation --out-dir /tmp/nixl_wheels \
-        --python ${PYTHON_VERSION} \
-        -Csetup-args=-Ducx_path=${UCX_HOME} \
-        -Csetup-args=-Dwheel_variant=rocm \
-        -Csetup-args=-Dbuild_tests=false \
-        -Csetup-args=-Dbuild_examples=false && \
-    mkdir -p /tmp/nixl_wheels/repaired /app/install && \
-    auditwheel repair \
-        --exclude 'libamdhip64*' \
-        --exclude 'libcore*' \
-        --exclude 'libpull*' \
-        /tmp/nixl_wheels/nixl_rocm*.whl \
-        --plat manylinux_2_35_$(uname -m) \
-        --wheel-dir /tmp/nixl_wheels/repaired && \
-    ./contrib/wheel_add_ucx_plugins.py \
-        --ucx-plugins-dir ${UCX_HOME}/lib/ucx \
-        --nixl-plugins-dir ${NIXL_HOME}/lib/$(uname -m)-linux-gnu/plugins \
-        /tmp/nixl_wheels/repaired/*.whl && \
-    cp /tmp/nixl_wheels/repaired/*.whl /app/install
-
-# Fetch and verify pinned LMCache source.
-FROM base AS lmcache_source
-ARG LMCACHE_REPO="https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache.git"
-ARG LMCACHE_REF="140819c9d57a975dbc5678a6459a218e544cb58b"
-ARG LMCACHE_VERSION="0.5.3"
-
-# Remove NVIDIA-only dependencies and accept the release image's NumPy version.
-RUN printf '%s\n' "${LMCACHE_REF}" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{40}$' \

-ARG LMCACHE_VERSION="0.5.3"

-        | grep -Eq '^gfx[0-9a-z]+(;gfx[0-9a-z]+)*$'; \

-# ROCShmem build stage - split from DeepEP so changing DEEPEP_BRANCH does not
-# invalidate the slow ROCShmem build.
-FROM base AS build_rocshmem

-ARG ROCSHMEM_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems.git"

-# it can be linked against DeepEP without arch mismatches.
-ARG DEEPEP_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
-ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm
-ENV ROCSHMEM_DIR=/opt/rocshmem

-RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/ccache \
-    git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none ${ROCSHMEM_REPO} \
- && cd rocm-systems \
- && git sparse-checkout set --cone projects/rocshmem \
- && git checkout ${ROCSHMEM_BRANCH} \
- && mkdir -p projects/rocshmem/build \
- && cd projects/rocshmem/build \
- && CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++" INSTALL_PREFIX=${ROCSHMEM_DIR} \
-    bash ../scripts/build_configs/all_backends \
-      -DROCM_PATH=${ROCM_PATH} \
-      -DGPU_TARGETS="${DEEPEP_ROCM_ARCH}" \
-      -DUSE_EXTERNAL_MPI=OFF

-# DeepEP build stage - depends on ROCShmem, builds the HIP kernel wheel.
-FROM build_rocshmem AS build_deepep
-ARG DEEPEP_BRANCH="0f63d3e9"
-ARG DEEPEP_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/DeepEP.git"
-ARG DEEPEP_NIC="cx7"

-# quantization bound with vLLM's own clamp

- && git clone ${DEEPEP_REPO} \
- && cd DeepEP \
- && git checkout ${DEEPEP_BRANCH} \
- && LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" MAX_JOBS="${MAX_JOBS:-$(nproc)}" python3 setup.py --variant rocm --rocm-explicit-ctx --nic ${DEEPEP_NIC} --rocm-gfx942-fp8-fnuz-max 224 bdist_wheel --dist-dir=/app/deep_install

-# MoRI runtime dependencies live in Dockerfile.rocm_72 so NIC backend changes do
-# not force users to rebuild the long-lived Dockerfile.rocm_72_base image.
-FROM base AS mori_base
-ARG NIC_BACKEND
-ARG AINIC_VERSION
-ARG UBUNTU_CODENAME
-RUN /bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail; \
- \
- install_ainic() { \
-   apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl gnupg apt-transport-https; \
-   rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
-   mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings; \
-   curl -fsSL https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/rocm.gpg.key | gpg --dearmor > /etc/apt/keyrings/amdainic.gpg; \
-   echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/amdainic.gpg] https://repo.radeon.com/amdainic/pensando/ubuntu/${AINIC_VERSION} ${UBUNTU_CODENAME} main" \
-     > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/amdainic.list; \
-   apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
-     libionic-dev \
-     ionic-common \
-   ; \
-   rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
- }; \
- \
- # NOTE: requires FW 235.2.86.0 and kernel drivers on the host: \
- #   bnxt-en-dkms=1.10.3.235.2.86.0 bnxt-re-dkms=235.2.86.0 (from packages.broadcom.com PPA) \
- install_bnxt() { \
-   install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings; \
-   curl -fsSL https://packages.broadcom.com/artifactory/api/security/keypair/PackagesKey/public \
-     -o /etc/apt/keyrings/broadcom-nic.asc; \
-   chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/broadcom-nic.asc; \
-   echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/broadcom-nic.asc] https://packages.broadcom.com/artifactory/ethernet-nic-debian-public jammy main" \
-     > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/broadcom-nic.list; \
-   apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
-     bnxt-rocelib=235.2.86.0 \
-   ; \
-   cp -a /usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libbnxt_re* /usr/local/lib/; \
-   ldconfig; \
-   rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
- }; \
- \
- echo "[MORI] Install MoRI proxy deps"; \
- pip install --quiet --ignore-installed blinker && \
- pip install --quiet quart msgpack aiohttp pyzmq; \
- echo "[MORI] NIC_BACKEND=${NIC_BACKEND}"; \
- \
- # NIC backend deps — mori auto-detects NIC at runtime (MORI_DEVICE_NIC env var override). \
- # Only vendor packages are installed here for dlopen; no compile-time flags needed. \
- case "${NIC_BACKEND}" in \
-   none)  ;; \
-   all)   install_ainic; install_bnxt ;; \
-   ainic) install_ainic ;; \
-   bnxt)  install_bnxt ;; \
-   *)     echo "ERROR: unknown NIC_BACKEND=${NIC_BACKEND}. Use one of: none, ainic, bnxt, all"; exit 2 ;; \
- esac'

-COPY --from=rust-build ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/vllm-rs ${COMMON_WORKDIR}/vllm/vllm/vllm-rs

-RUN mkdir -p /install

-        echo "Copied custom wheels:"; \

-# CI base image (Tier 1) - stable, rarely changing CI dependencies.
-# Per-PR test builds pull this as CI_BASE_IMAGE so the test stage only layers
-# in the vLLM artifacts for the current commit.
-FROM mori_base AS ci_base
-ARG COMMON_WORKDIR
-
-ENV CARGO_HOME=/root/.cargo
-ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/root/.rustup
-ENV PATH=${CARGO_HOME}/bin:${PATH}
-
-# Bake the Rust toolchain into ci_base so Rust build/test steps do not
-# need to fetch it on each per-commit image build.
-COPY --from=rust-toolchain /root/.cargo /root/.cargo
-COPY --from=rust-toolchain /root/.rustup /root/.rustup
-
-# Update rdma-core to support latest rocshmem.
-ARG DEEPEP_NIC
-RUN if [ "${DEEPEP_NIC}" = "cx7" ] || [ "${DEEPEP_NIC}" = "io" ]; then \
-    git clone --branch v62.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/linux-rdma/rdma-core.git /tmp/rdma-core && \
-    cd /tmp/rdma-core && \
-    mkdir -p build && cd build && \
-    cmake -GNinja -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr -DNO_MAN_PAGES=1 .. && \
-    ninja && ninja install && ldconfig && rm -rf /tmp/rdma-core; \

-# Install NIXL + DeepEP wheels.

-    -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30 \
-    -o Acquire::https::Timeout=30 \

-    libibverbs1 \
-    ibverbs-providers \
-    ibverbs-utils \
-    util-linux \
-    unzip \

+"""The AMD CI pytest plugin skips native teardown without changing pytest's result."""
+
+import os
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+PLUGIN_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci"
+
+# An object that segfaults when the interpreter tears its module down, after the
+# summary, as native library destructors did in vllm/ci #96786.
+CRASH_AT_TEARDOWN = """
+import faulthandler
+
+class _CrashOnTeardown:
+    def __del__(self, _crash=faulthandler._sigsegv):
+        _crash()
+
+_keep = _CrashOnTeardown()
+"""
+
+
+def _run(tmp_path, body, *, plugin=True, env=None, args=()):
+    (tmp_path / "test_case.py").write_text(CRASH_AT_TEARDOWN + body)
+    run_env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "PYTEST_ADDOPTS"}
+    for name in ("ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES", "CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH", "VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT"):
+        run_env.pop(name, None)
+    run_env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(PLUGIN_DIR)
+    run_env.update(env or {})
+    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *args]
+    if plugin:
+        cmd += ["-p", "amd_ci_fast_exit"]
+    return subprocess.run(
+        [*cmd, "test_case.py"],
+        cwd=tmp_path,
+        env=run_env,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+
+
+PASSING = "\ndef test_ok():\n    assert True\n"
+
+
+def test_reproduces_the_teardown_crash_without_the_plugin(tmp_path):
+    assert _run(tmp_path, PASSING, plugin=False).returncode == -signal.SIGSEGV
+
+
+def test_a_passing_run_exits_zero_despite_the_teardown_crash(tmp_path):
+    result = _run(tmp_path, PASSING)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    assert "leaving without native teardown" in result.stderr

+def context_sources(dockerfile: str) -> set[str]:
+    text = dockerfile.replace("\\\n", " ")
+    srcs = set()
+    for args in re.findall(r"^\s*(?:COPY|ADD)\s+(.*)$", text, re.M):
+        words = [w for w in args.split() if not w.startswith("--")]
+        if "--from=" not in args and not words[0].startswith("http"):
+            srcs.update(words[:-1])
+    for opts in re.findall(r"--mount=type=bind,(\S*)", text):
+        kv = dict(o.partition("=")[::2] for o in opts.split(","))
+        if "from" not in kv:
+            srcs.add(kv.get("source", kv.get("src", ".")))
+    return srcs

+def key_paths(name: str, stack: str = "") -> set[str]:
+    script = (ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh").read_text()
+    block_match = re.search(rf"^{name}=\$\(.*?sha256sum", script, re.M | re.S)
+    assert block_match is not None, f"{name}= block not found in build.sh"
+    pattern = r"\b(?:requirements|tools|tests)/[\w./-]+|\brust-toolchain\.toml\b"
+    paths = set(re.findall(pattern, block_match.group(0)))
+    # therock_wheels.py is injected into Ks via a helper variable (rocm stack only)
+    if name == "Ks" and stack == "rocm":
+        m = re.search(r"_[Tt][Rr][Ww]=.*?tools/[\w./-]+", script, re.S)
+        if m:
+            paths.update(re.findall(r"\b(?:requirements|tools)/[\w./-]+", m.group(0)))
+    return paths

 For CPU resource sizing recommendations, see
 [CPU Resources for GPU Deployments](../configuration/optimization.md#cpu-resources-for-gpu-deployments).
 
+## Scheduler
+
+The scheduler runs inside the **Engine Core Process** and decides which
+requests execute each step. The code can be found in
+[vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py).
+
+The scheduler is **token-budget-based**: each step, it fills a budget of
+`max_num_batched_tokens` across both running and waiting requests. There are no
+separate prefill and decode phases. Each request tracks how many of its tokens
+have been computed, and the scheduler assigns it tokens to close the gap. This
+single loop handles chunked prefill, prefix caching and speculative decoding.
+
+### Scheduling Policies
+
+Two policies are supported via `--scheduling-policy`:
+
+- **FCFS** (default): requests are scheduled first-come, first-served. When
+    the KV cache is exhausted, the last-admitted running request is preempted.
+- **Priority**: requests carry an integer `priority` field. When the KV cache
+    is exhausted, the running request with the lowest priority (highest
+    `priority` value, then latest arrival time) is preempted.
+
+### Preemption
+
+When a request cannot be allocated new KV cache blocks, the scheduler
+**preempts** running requests, chosen by the scheduling policy, until enough
+blocks are free:
+
+1. The preempted request's KV cache blocks are freed.
+2. Its progress is reset and it returns to the waiting queue. Under FCFS it
+    goes to the front of the queue; under Priority it is reinserted by
+    `(priority, arrival_time)`.
+3. When re-admitted, it is recomputed rather than swapped back from CPU
+    memory. Prefix caching or a KV connector can restore part of its progress
+    immediately.
+
+For how to reduce preemption, see
+[Preemption](../configuration/optimization.md#preemption).
+
+### Async Scheduling
+
+With async scheduling,
+[vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py)
+overlaps CPU scheduling with GPU execution: while the GPU executes step *N*,
+the CPU schedules step *N+1*, using placeholders for the tokens that step *N*
+will produce.
+
+If a request is preempted while it still has output in flight, that output is
+normally still delivered when it arrives. It is dropped instead when delivering
+it would be invalid, for example when `reset_prefix_cache` preempts and resumes
+requests within the same step.
+

+def _resolve_prompt_logprobs(
+    prompt_logprobs: PromptLogprobs | None, tokenizer: TokenizerLike
+) -> PromptLogprobs | None:
+    """Fill missing ``decoded_token`` values in prompt logprobs.
+
+    A ``--tokens-only`` generate server has no tokenizer, so it returns
+    ``decoded_token=None``. Mirrors LogprobsProcessor._update_prompt_logprobs
+    in v1/engine/logprobs.py: decode each token id, then fix U+FFFD using the
+    preceding prompt tokens (the first entry of each earlier position).
+    """
+    if prompt_logprobs is None:
+        return None
+
+    missing = list(
+        dict.fromkeys(
+            tid
+            for entry in prompt_logprobs
+            if entry is not None
+            for tid, lp in entry.items()
+            if lp.decoded_token is None
+        )
+    )
+    if not missing:
+        return prompt_logprobs
+    # Ids with no vocab entry decode to "", as for output logprobs.
+    decoded = {
+        tid: text
+        for tid, (text, _) in zip(missing, decode_token_ids(missing, tokenizer))
+    }
+
+    resolved: PromptLogprobs = []
+    context_token_ids: list[int] = []
+    for entry in prompt_logprobs:
+        if not entry:
+            resolved.append(entry)
+            continue
+        new_entry: dict[int, Logprob] = {}
+        for tid, lp in entry.items():
+            if lp.decoded_token is None:
+                text = decoded[tid]
+                if text.endswith("\ufffd"):
+                    text = _correct_decoded_token(tid, context_token_ids, tokenizer)
+                lp = Logprob(lp.logprob, lp.rank, text)
+            new_entry[tid] = lp
+        resolved.append(new_entry)
+        # The prompt token is always inserted first by the engine.
+        context_token_ids.append(next(iter(entry)))
+    return resolved
+
